sourcedFrom: NOMAX 33 OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: ⛔ Read the last line of this guide first: Dead Air publishes NO cleaning or maintenance section for the Nomax 33. What its book does publish is a modular mounting system — Direct Thread, Xemax, Xeno and KeyMo adapters, an R-Series front cap, and hook spanner wrenches to move them — plus a rate-of-fire limit that is unusually specific. Everything below is that, and nothing is invented to fill the gap where a cleaning section would be.

steps.title: ⛔ .33 XC / .338 Lapua Magnum — and a TEN ROUNDS PER MINUTE limit
steps.action: Before anything else, read the rating. Unless the can or its packaging says otherwise, the Nomax 33 will not function safely above .33 XC and .338 Lapua Magnum with a 26-inch barrel, and Dead Air sets a hard cadence: DO NOT EXCEED MORE THAN 10 ROUNDS PER MINUTE. 8.6 Blackout subsonic needs at least an 8-inch barrel; supersonic 8.6 keeps the 10 rpm cap on a 12.5-inch barrel.
steps.prose: A rate-of-fire ceiling is rarer than a pressure ceiling and it is the one that gets exceeded without anyone noticing.
steps.quote: OUR PRODUCTS ARE CALIBER SPECIFIC. UNLESS STATED OTHERWISE ON THE SUPPRESSOR ITSELF OR ON THE PACKAGING, THE SUPPRESSOR WILL NOT FUNCTION SAFELY WITH ANY CARTRIDGE WITH PRESSURES HIGHER THAN .33 XC AND .338 LAPUA MAGNUM WITH A BARREL LENGTH OF 26 INCHES. DO NOT EXCEED MORE THAN 10 ROUNDS PER MINUTE.
steps.cite: NOMAX 33 OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Installation and Removal, Step One, p.9

steps.title: Cold, clear, and know which way your barrel thread turns
steps.action: Let the can cool and prove the host empty before you handle either. Then confirm the barrel thread: Dead Air notes that some threads are left-handed and turn the opposite way to what you expect, and that the matching Direct Thread Adapter or muzzle device must be the one fitted in the suppressor.
steps.prose: On a .338-class can the joints are tight and the torque is real. Turning a left-hand thread the wrong way once is enough.
steps.quote: Note that some threads are left-handed, meaning they turn the opposite direction than what you may be used to.
steps.cite: NOMAX 33 OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Installation and Removal, Step Two, p.10
steps.warn: THE SUPPRESSOR MAY BECOME EXTREMELY HOT AFTER USE. NEVER GRAB A HOT SUPPRESSOR AS IT CAN RESULT IN BURNS AND INJURY.

steps.title: Off the barrel — body counter-clockwise, spanner if it is hot
steps.action: Rotate the body of the suppressor counter-clockwise until it unthreads from the muzzle (clockwise if the thread is left-handed). With a KeyMo adapter fitted it is different: rotate the body counter-clockwise about three-quarters of a full turn until it stops, then slip it off the brake or flash hider.
steps.prose: Two removals for one can, depending on what is on the back of it. Know which you have before you start turning.
steps.aside: The Hook Spanner wrench may be used to loosen a suppressor that’s too hot to touch.
steps.quote: To remove the suppressor with the Key-Mo adapter installed, simply rotate the body counter-clockwise approximately ¾ of full turn at which point it will stop turning.
steps.cite: NOMAX 33 OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Installation and Removal, Step Three, p.10

steps.title: ⚠ Adapter out — hook spanners opposed, and MIND THE PINCH POINT
steps.action: Catch the notches with the Hook Spanner wrenches so the ADAPTER turns counter-clockwise and the SUPPRESSOR turns clockwise, with an inch or two between the handles for leverage, and squeeze them together. ⛔ When the torque breaks, the wrenches swing toward each other and your fingers are in the gap.
steps.prose: Dead Air writes "mind the gap" in its own warning. It means the gap between the two handles.
steps.quote: Use the Hook Spanners to catch the notches in the parts such that the adapter is being turned Counter-Clockwise and the suppressor Clock- wise.
steps.cite: NOMAX 33 OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Adapter Removal, Step One, p.7
steps.warn: YOU MAY NEED TO HEAT THE SUPPRESSOR UP TO LOOSEN THE THREADS. PAY SPECIAL ATTENTION TO THE HEATED SURFACES TO AVOID BURNS! WHEN THE TORQUE BREAKS BETWEEN THE TWO PARTS, THE WRENCHES MAY SWING ENOUGH TO CREATE A PINCH POINT. ALWAYS BE CAREFUL AND MIND THE GAP!

steps.title: Front cap off — DA208 pins fully engaged, counter-clockwise
steps.action: Align the pins of the Sandman Front Cap Tool (DA208, sold separately) into the holes cut in the front cap. Get the tool FLAT against the cap with the pins evenly and fully engaged, then apply torque counter-clockwise to loosen and remove.
steps.prose: Flat and fully engaged is the whole instruction — a pin part-way into a hole rounds the hole and then there is no way in at all.
steps.quote: Align the pins in the Sandman Front Cap Tool (DA208—sold separately) into the holes cut into the front cap. Ensure tool is flat against the front cap with the pins evenly and fully engaged and apply torque Counter-Clockwise to loosen and remove.
steps.cite: NOMAX 33 OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Front Cap Installation, Step One, p.8

steps.title: Threads and taper — that is what this book gives you
steps.action: Clean the threads and the taper, and apply a high-quality grease to those surfaces before the cap goes back and is hand-tightened. Do the same wherever an adapter has been out: clean threads, high-quality grease, then reassemble.
steps.prose: This sentence is the closest thing to a cleaning instruction in the whole book, and it is about mating surfaces, not about fouling.
steps.quote: STEP TWO: Clean threads and taper. Apply high quality grease to the surfaces and install new cap and hand tighten.
steps.cite: NOMAX 33 OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Front Cap Installation, Step Two, p.8

steps.title: Adapter back in — grease, bottom it out, spanners opposed
steps.action: Coat the chosen adapter's threads with high-quality grease and thread it into the suppressor until it bottoms out on the rear suppressor face. Then hook spanners: adapter CLOCKWISE, suppressor COUNTER-clockwise, an inch or two between the handles. ⚠ A HUB Taper adapter bottoms on an internal taper instead, which leaves a visible gap at the flange — that gap is correct, not a fault.
steps.prose: Knowing the gap is by design is what stops someone torquing it away and damaging the taper.
steps.quote: Note: Adapter options that incorporate HUB Taper architecture will bottom out on a taper inside the rear of the suppressor rather than on the rear suppressor face, resulting in a gap between the front face of the notched flange and the rear suppressor face.
steps.cite: NOMAX 33 OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Adapter Installation, Step Two, p.6

steps.title: Onto the barrel HAND TIGHT — 25 ±5 ft-lb, never over 30
steps.action: Clean and lube the barrel threads, then thread the can on carefully — hand tightening is Dead Air's preference, with a hook spanner for a little extra if you want it. Barrel torque for Key-Mount and Xeno devices and Direct Thread Adapters must not exceed 30 ft-lbs; 25 ±5 is the target. ⛔ Do not thread onto a barrel with no proper shoulder or a muzzle face that is not square to the bore.
steps.prose: Over-tightening this joint damages the firearm, the can, or both — and it buys nothing, because the seat is the shoulder.
steps.caution: Check tightness often — all direct thread suppressors loosen with use.
steps.quote: Barrel Torque for both Key-Mount and Xeno muzzle devices and Direct Thread Adapters shall not exceed 30 ft-lbs. A target of 25 +/- 5 ft-lbs. is optimal.
steps.cite: NOMAX 33 OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Installation and Removal, Step Two, p.10

steps.title: Snug, no rattle — and a HUB taper gap is the exception
steps.action: Everything should be snug with no rattling and no gaps, UNLESS a HUB Taper adapter is fitted, where the flange gap above is expected. Anything else loose means damaged threads or debris: clean both mating parts and tighten again rather than forcing it.
steps.prose: One documented exception to "no gaps" on this can. Everything else that gaps is a fault.
steps.quote: STEP FOUR: INSPECTION UPON ASSEMBLY All components should be snug with no rattling, or no gaps, unless otherwise noted by use of HUB Taper adapters.
steps.cite: NOMAX 33 OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Installation and Removal, Step Four, p.10
steps.warn: NOTE: DEBRIS ON THE THREADS AND TAPER SURFACES MAY CAUSE MISALIGNMENT OF SUPPRESSOR PARTS AND ALLOW FOR PROJECTILE STRIKES ON BAFFLES OR THE FRONT CAP.

deepAbsentReason: Dead Air's Nomax 33 manual publishes NO cleaning or maintenance section at all. Its eleven sections are Product Overview, General Considerations, Adapter Installation, Adapter Removal, Front Cap Installation, Inspection Upon Assembly, Installation and Removal, Disclaimer, Warranty, Lawful Use and Possession, and Contact Information. The only cleaning sentence anywhere in the book is "Clean threads and taper" before greasing and refitting the front cap. No baffle service, no solvent, no ultrasonic guidance and no interval is published for this model, so none is written here. This listing therefore has NO deep clean.
reassembly: Adapter threads greased; adapter bottomed on the rear face (or on the HUB taper).
Hook spanners: adapter clockwise, suppressor counter-clockwise, handles an inch apart.
Front cap threads and taper cleaned and greased; cap hand tight with the DA208 pins flat.
Barrel threads clean and lubed; can hand tight against the shoulder.
25 ±5 ft-lb on the mount, never past 30.
Snug with no rattle — a HUB taper flange gap is expected and correct.
fncheck: Mount it and inspect visually that the can is straight to the centreline of the bore and not canted. If it is not in line, STOP and contact Dead Air — firing an improperly mounted can causes irreparable harm to it. Confirm the can is tight against the shoulder, that nothing rattles, and ⛔ confirm your intended cadence against the 10 rounds-per-minute limit before the first string, not after it.
